partner_context.their_ambition: Universal Resorts opened the Maldives to the world — the country's first resort, Kurumba, in 1972 — and built a portfolio of owned island properties (Kurumba, Baros, Velassaru, Huvafen Fushi, Milaidhoo) defined by understated, design-led luxury. As the original asset owner of Maldivian tourism, its ambition is to keep the arrival experience as refined as the islands themselves.
partner_context.their_pressure: Across an owned portfolio, the transfer is the one part of the guest journey Universal does not fully control: seaplanes are weather- and daylight-limited and loud, diesel speedboats are rough, and both undercut the calm, design-forward arrival its resorts are known for. For an asset owner, that inconsistency is a portfolio-wide liability, not a one-resort problem.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Because Universal owns its islands, it can re-platform arrivals across the whole portfolio at once. A shared N35 foiling fleet turns the transfer into a branded, all-weather, zero-emission arrival product — the same calm, quiet quality on every island, controlled end to end.

hero.title: Navier × Universal Resorts — arrival as a product, across the owned portfolio
hero.subtitle: Re-platforming the airport-to-jetty transfer on foiling-electric vessels — silent, all-weather, zero-emission.
hero.what_we_do_together: Navier and Universal Resorts bring a foiling-electric arrival layer to its Maldivian islands. Navier supplies the software-defined N35 fleet, captain training and the certification path; Universal Resorts brings the resort relationships and the rollout sequence across its owned portfolio. The transfer stops being the weakest link in a premium stay and becomes a branded, all-weather, zero-emission arrival — the same calm quality on every island.

why_now: The Navier × JIH Global program — ~100 vessels, $100M, a three-year phased rollout with the first 5 boats in 2026 — proves, publicly and in Maldivian waters, that foiling-electric works at scale. For Universal Resorts, that removes the risk: the platform is real and ramping, and the only question is which of its islands to re-platform first.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots between Velana International and the Universal Resorts jetty — the highest-value leg of the guest journey — with seaplane retained only for the longest outer-atoll legs. The resort books and brands the experience; guests step from jet to foil to villa.

journeys_unlocked.today: 20–45 min in a diesel speedboat, rough in any swell, or a costly seaplane hop.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A smooth, silent ~25-minute foiling transfer direct to the resort jetty — any weather, after dark.

journeys_unlocked.today: Seaplane only — daylight-limited, weather-cancelled, ~$600+ round trip.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: An all-weather, after-dark foiling link to the mid-atolls, complementing seaplane for the longest legs.

journeys_unlocked.today: Congested causeway road or a slow public ferry.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: A fast foiling commuter and visitor link across the capital's lagoon — the resident layer of the same program.

journeys_unlocked.today: A slow tender or a charter booked hours ahead.
journeys_unlocked.with_navier: On-demand premium island-hopping between islands, sandbanks and dive sites — the quiet in-stay water layer.

differentiation.why_navier: Universal opened the Maldives in 1972 and still owns the islands it pioneered — Kurumba, Baros, Velassaru, Huvafen Fushi, Milaidhoo. Navier re-platforms the arrival for that founding portfolio, holding the same understated, design-led standard that defines the islands and extending it to the boat that brings guests there.

proof_points.claim: Foiling-electric is already deploying at national scale in the Maldives.
proof_points.evidence: Navier × JIH Global: ~100 vessels / $100M / three-year phasing; first 5 boats in 2026.

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

proof_points.claim: As the original asset owner, Universal controls the whole journey — except the boat.
proof_points.evidence: Universal owns its islands and their design language end to end; re-platforming the transfer is the last piece of the guest journey it doesn't yet control to the same standard.

proof_points.claim: A design-led group should arrive on a design-led vessel.
proof_points.evidence: The understated luxury that defines Kurumba and Baros is undercut by a loud seaplane or speedboat; a silent foiling arrival keeps the standard consistent from jetty to suite.

objections.concern: We pioneered these islands — why change a transfer that works?
objections.response: It works, but it's the one part of the journey that doesn't yet meet Universal's own design standard. A silent, all-weather foiling arrival at Kurumba or Baros is the last upgrade to a guest journey Universal otherwise owns end to end.

objections.concern: Can it handle the crossings and swell to the owned islands?
objections.response: The foil flies above the chop for a smoother ride than a diesel speedboat; the N35's enclosed all-weather cabin keeps the arrival composed, and the Quanta-LR hybrid covers the longer legs to Huvafen Fushi or Milaidhoo with no charging infrastructure.

objections.concern: What about charging at the resort jetties?
objections.response: The N35 needs only a berth pedestal at the Kurumba or Baros jetty; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs none — so re-platforming the portfolio is not gated on island infrastructure.

phases.label: Phase 1 — flagship-island pilot
phases.narrative: A focused pilot on Universal Resorts's busiest airport-to-jetty corridor — proving the all-weather N35 arrival on the island where the most guests will feel it.
phases.rationale: Start where transfer volume is highest and the arrival impression matters most.

phases.narrative: Scale the N35 arrival across Universal Resorts's islands and add Quanta-LR for the longer inter-property and outer-atoll legs — one branded, all-weather, zero-emission arrival layer spanning the whole owned portfolio.

phases.rationale: Complete the three-year phased rollout to national coverage — the full realisation of the signed program.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined N35 foiling fleet, captain training, the maintenance and certification path, and an operating playbook already being proven in Maldivian waters.
the_ask.partner_brings: Resort relationships across its owned portfolio, the island-by-island rollout sequence, jetty access and the guest-experience standard.
the_ask.next_step: Select Universal Resorts's first flagship island for a foiling-arrival pilot and define the portfolio rollout sequence.

close.title: The arrival, finally as good as the stay.
close.body: For Universal Resorts, the transfer has always been the one part of the journey that didn't match the islands. Foiling-electric closes that gap — a silent, all-weather, zero-emission arrival, the same quality on every island.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop — roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. Software-defined and autonomy-ready, the same fleet keeps improving over time.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists — the open ocean and the resort jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way. The N35 needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all.
why_navier_now.the_moment: Decarbonization expectations turned diesel transfer fleets into a liability, the platform crossed from prototype to proven service, and a national-scale Maldives program is already live — the resort arrival layer is being re-platformed right now.

end_state.headline: A branded foiling arrival layer across the Universal Resorts owned portfolio.
end_state.addressable_footprint: Every Universal Resorts island in the Maldives, connected to Velana International and to each other by a fast, silent, zero-emission foiling fleet.

steady_state.total_corridors: Airport-to-jetty arrivals + inter-property and in-stay hops
steady_state.platform_mix: N35 for resort arrivals; Pioneer II for short in-stay hops; Quanta-LR for the longest inter-property legs
steady_state.tam_framing: Every guest arrival and in-stay transfer across the portfolio, re-platformed as one branded fleet.

end_state.narrative: Steady state is a Universal Resorts-branded foiling arrival network: jet-to-foil-to-villa on every island, the same calm quality end to end.
